newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -STG VOLS RISE AHEAD OF BOE RATE DECISION.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -STG VOLS RISE AHEAD OF BOE RATE DECISION.

text.p: Sterling volatilities were sharply higher ahead of the outcome of today's Bank of England monetary policy committee meeting.

"Opinion on whether UK rates will be raised is pretty divided now and in any case the market is expecting a lot of volatility. This has seen prices up but not a lot of activity today," said a U.S. bank dealer.
Spot sterling was steadier against the dollar and mark after Wednesday's sell-off but vols were marked up ahead of today's announcement.
One-month cable vol stood at 10.1/10.4 percent against 8.85/9.15 percent Wednesday and sterling/mark vol was trading at 11.4/11.7 from 10.6/11.1 percent.
Dollar option volatilities were trading lower at the European midsession, tracking spot's consolidation from Wednesday's highs.

Dealers said dollar spot's failure to hold Wednesday's key levels -- 1.89 in dollar/mark and 119 in dollar/yen -- prompted a retracement in volatility as the market sees tighter ranges into the weekend.

"Vols were getting pretty rich yesterday so it wasn't too surprising to see some of that froth getting sold-off," said a UK bank dealer. "But there's no sign yet of a reversal in trend, vols still look well-bid."

One-month dollar/mark volatility stood at 11.5/11.75 percent against 11.65/12.00 late Wednesday. The risk reversal, the difference in implied volatility between calls relative to puts, was steady at 0.5/0.8 percent for mark puts.
Dollar/yen's spot dip below 119 also saw vols trading lower with one-month now at 11.5/11.8 percent from 12.4/12.7 Wednesday. One-year vols also came off to 12.3/12.5 versus 12.7/13.2 percent.
Mark/yen's downtrend continued, pushing to a new two-year low in early trade which served to push vols ever higher. The one-month ticked up to 11.5/12.0 percent from 11.3/11.7.
